passage: Note from the class teacher. Today I saw Uday throw a paper plane and told him off. He went silent and scowled at his shoes, arms crossed, and would not join the drawing. When I sat by him later he said, "Harsha threw one too and you only said me." I had not seen Harsha's. I thanked Uday for telling me and said I was sorry I had not looked at both. Then I spoke to the two of them together. Uday's frown eased a little.

qa.q: What did Uday throw before the teacher told him off?
What was Uday feeling when he scowled and sat with crossed arms?
qa.a: He felt that being told off alone was unfair, and he was cross and hurt. His silence shows how much.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped, and what could Uday try next time?
qa.a: They sat by him, listened to his side, thanked him and apologised for not looking at both. Uday could speak up sooner, without sulking, if he thinks it is unfair.

qa.q: How might Harsha have felt when the teacher spoke to Uday and Harsha together?
qa.a: Harsha may have been uneasy, relieved or a bit guilty at being included. It was fairer because both had done the same thing.

grounding: I was scolded for something my friend also did; it feels unfair and I go quiet, and a wise adult listens to my side.
